indicator_definition: This indicator measures the difference between the proportion of men and women aged 16 to 74 who used the internet in the last three months, expressed in percentage points. A positive value indicates higher internet use among men. Data are collected through the EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals.
rationale: The digital gender gap reflects broader inequalities in access to technology, information and economic opportunities. Closing the gap requires targeted policies to improve digital access, skills and confidence among women. Progress means a reduction in the difference between male and female internet use rates.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals, conducted annually. Internet use refers to use of the internet for any purpose in the three months preceding the survey. The gender gap is calculated as the difference between male and female internet use rates, expressed in percentage points.
